subject: science
title: Life Around Us · Q2 W03 D05
objective: Classify familiar examples as living or non-living and describe basic needs or body parts.
introduction: A butterfly flutters by, and a cow grazes in the field. The stone on the path just sits there — is it living?

items.explanation: A butterfly grows, eats, and drinks, so it is living. A rock, water, and a pencil do not grow.

items.prompt: Which is NOT a living thing?
items.explanation: A stone does not grow and does not need food or water, so it is not living. The duck, the butterfly, and the cow are living.

items.prompt: What do all living things need to grow?
items.explanation: Living things need food and water to grow and stay alive. Covers, shelves, and batteries are not food or water.

items.prompt: What does a dog need to live?
items.explanation: A dog needs food and water to live and grow. Batteries, plastic bags, and remotes are not food or water.

items.prompt: Which example shows a living thing?
items.explanation: A cow grows, needs food and water, and can have calves, so it is living. A stone, water, and a pencil are not.
